title: Nuclear-Free Constitution Approved by Referendum
description: Palauans approved the world's first nuclear-free constitution by 92 percent in July 1979, banning nuclear weapons, waste and propulsion in Palauan territory. The provision required a 75 percent majority to override and would delay the Compact of Free Association for 15 years.

title: Republic of Palau Constitution Enters Force
description: The Republic of Palau formally took over self-government on 1 January 1981 with Haruo Remeliik as first president. Palau remained under US trusteeship pending Compact ratification.

title: First Compact Plebiscite Fails Supermajority Threshold
description: A February 1983 plebiscite on the Compact of Free Association won majority support but fell short of the 75 percent needed to override the nuclear-free constitution. It was the first of seven referendums over the next decade.

title: President Haruo Remeliik Assassinated
description: Founding President Haruo Remeliik was assassinated outside his home on 30 June 1985, in the only successful presidential assassination in modern Pacific history. Three men were convicted but later acquitted on appeal, leaving the case unresolved.

title: Lazarus Salii Becomes President
description: Lazarus Salii won the special presidential election held after Remeliik's assassination. Salii inherited the politically volatile Compact-ratification process amid intense divisions over the nuclear ban.

title: Constitutional Override Amendment Falls
description: Palauans rejected a constitutional amendment that would have lowered the supermajority required to approve the Compact, blocking another path to ratification. Tensions over the issue grew increasingly violent.

title: President Lazarus Salii Found Dead
description: President Lazarus Salii was found dead from a gunshot wound on 20 August 1988 in what was officially ruled suicide amid a corruption scandal. Persistent doubts about the cause of death contributed to lingering political unease.

title: Ngiratkel Etpison Elected President
description: Ngiratkel Etpison narrowly defeated Roman Tmetuchl to become the third elected president of Palau in November 1988, taking office in January 1989. He continued seeking a path to ratify the Compact.

title: Kuniwo Nakamura Elected President
description: Kuniwo Nakamura defeated Johnson Toribiong to win the presidency in November 1992. His political skill and diplomatic patience would finally deliver the Compact two years later.

title: Eighth Compact Plebiscite Succeeds
description: After a separate constitutional amendment lowered the supermajority threshold to a simple majority for the Compact specifically, Palauans approved the agreement in November 1993. The vote ended 15 years of stalemate.

title: Compact of Free Association Enters Force
description: The Compact of Free Association with the United States entered into force on 1 October 1994, granting full sovereignty while reserving US defence rights and providing 50 years of grant funding and economic assistance. Palau became the last Trust Territory to gain independence.

title: Palau Admitted to the United Nations
description: Palau joined the United Nations on 15 December 1994 as the 185th member, completing decolonisation of the Pacific Trust Territories. UN membership formalised Palau's sovereign international identity.

title: Diplomatic Recognition of Taiwan Cemented
description: Palau formally established diplomatic relations with the Republic of China (Taiwan) in December 1999. The relationship has produced steady aid flows and high-level exchanges and has held firm despite intense Chinese pressure.

title: Tommy Remengesau Jr. Elected President
description: Tommy Remengesau Jr. defeated Peter Sugiyama in November 2000 to become president, taking office in January 2001. His administration emphasised tourism, marine conservation and US ties.

title: Babeldaob Compact Road Completed
description: The 85-kilometre Compact-funded road circling Babeldaob Island opened in 2002, connecting outlying states to the new national capital area. The road was the largest infrastructure project in Palauan history.

title: Capital Moved to Ngerulmud
description: Palau formally moved its national capital from Koror to Ngerulmud in Melekeok State in 2006. The move fulfilled a constitutional mandate that the capital be on the larger Babeldaob Island.

title: Palau Accepts Uyghur Detainees from Guantanamo
description: Palau agreed in 2009 to resettle six ethnic Uyghur detainees released from US Guantanamo Bay custody, drawing strong protests from Beijing. The decision underscored Palau's pro-US alignment.

title: Shark Sanctuary Declared
description: Palau declared the world's first national shark sanctuary in 2009, banning all commercial shark fishing in its 600,000-square-kilometre exclusive economic zone. The move launched Palau's reputation as a global marine-conservation leader.

title: Tommy Remengesau Jr. Returns to Presidency
description: Tommy Remengesau Jr. returned to the presidency after defeating Surangel Whipps Jr. in November 2012. His second tenure focused on the marine sanctuary and Compact-funding renewal.

title: Palau National Marine Sanctuary Established
description: Parliament passed legislation in October 2015 designating 80 percent of Palau's exclusive economic zone as a fully protected marine sanctuary, the world's sixth largest. Implementation began in 2020 after a phase-out for existing licences.

title: Palau Pledge Required of All Visitors
description: Palau introduced the world's first eco-conservation passport pledge in December 2017, requiring all incoming visitors to commit in writing to preserving the country's natural environment. The initiative drew global attention.

title: Restrictions on Reef-Toxic Sunscreen Adopted
description: Palau passed legislation in 2018 banning sunscreens containing ingredients harmful to coral reefs, the first nationwide ban of its kind. The law took effect on 1 January 2020.

title: Tourism Slump After China Group-Travel Pressure
description: Reported Chinese restrictions on group tour packages to Palau, linked to Taiwan recognition, contributed to a sharp drop in tourist arrivals from 2018. The slump exposed Palau's tourism dependence and strengthened its pivot toward higher-value visitors.

title: Surangel Whipps Jr. Elected President
description: Surangel Whipps Jr., a businessman and brother-in-law of Remengesau, was elected president in November 2020. He took office in January 2021 facing the COVID-19 tourism collapse and Compact renewal.

title: COVID-19 Border Closure
description: Palau closed borders in March 2020 and remained one of the world's last COVID-free jurisdictions for nearly two years. Tourism, the main private-sector employer, collapsed and required US Compact-funded fiscal support.

title: Taiwan-Palau Travel Bubble Launched
description: Palau and Taiwan launched the Pacific's first quarantine-free travel bubble in April 2021 to revive tourism amid the pandemic. The bubble carried strong symbolic weight given the Taiwan diplomatic relationship.

title: First COVID-19 Outbreak in Community
description: Palau confirmed its first community outbreak of COVID-19 in early 2022 after years of zero cases. Vaccination uptake was among the highest in the world and the outbreak's mortality remained low.

title: Compact of Free Association Renegotiation Agreed
description: Palau and the United States agreed in May 2023 on a renewed 20-year Compact funding package worth roughly USD 890 million. US Congressional appropriation followed in March 2024 after months of delay.

title: Surangel Whipps Jr. Wins Re-election
description: President Surangel Whipps Jr. defeated former president Tommy Remengesau Jr. in a tight November 2024 election to win a second term. The campaign featured high-profile debates over Taiwan recognition and Chinese economic pressure.

title: Cyberattack Exposes Government Records
description: A major ransomware attack in 2024, attributed by some analysts to Chinese-linked actors, breached Palauan government records and exposed sensitive documents. The incident accelerated cybersecurity cooperation with US, Australian and Taiwanese partners.

title: Compact Funding Disbursed
description: The first tranches of the renewed Compact funding flowed to Palau after US Congressional appropriation in March 2024, restoring fiscal stability. The renewal ran through fiscal year 2044 with built-in adjustment mechanisms.

title: Marine Sanctuary Enforcement Strengthened
description: Palau commissioned a new offshore patrol vessel donated by Japan and accepted Australian and US assistance for satellite surveillance of its marine sanctuary in 2025. Illegal Chinese fishing incursions remained a recurring concern.
